ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the permanence and intensity of punishment in Hell?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the finality of divine justice for those who persist in disbelief, emphasizing that their punishment is neither mitigated nor postponed. The phrase 'la yunzharoon' (no respite) signifies a complete cessation of the period of trial, marking the transition from the world of action to the world of recompense. This reinforces the concept of 'Adl' (Divine Justice), where the severity of the punishment corresponds precisely to the magnitude of the sin without arbitrary reduction.

en.ahmedali: They shall live under it, and none of their agony decrease nor be respite for them.
en.ahmedraza: Remaining in it forever; their punishment will not be lightened,
nor will they get any respite.
en.arberry: therein dwelling forever; the chastisement shall not be lightened for them;
no respite shall be given them.

nor will it be delayed or postponed (for a while).
en.itani: Remaining in it eternally, without their punishment being eased from them,

nor shall they be granted any respite.
